title: Customer inference glance and recovery choices (draft)
content:
DRAFT - customer-facing brief + options (compact)

Title: Inference quality regression in EU region - glance, choices, and evidence pack
Date: 2028-04-02 (update: 2028-04-04)
Audience: impacted tenant admins, integrations teams, SRE and platform contacts

TL;DR
- What happened: Between 2028-04-01 22:13 UTC and 2028-04-02 06:48 UTC we observed a regression in generated responses for a subset of requests routed to EU inference capacity (higher truncation rates and repeated tokens). Root cause under investigation: cache-key collision during a routing rollout that produced stale KV cache hits for quantized model variants.
- Impact: ~0.7% of total inference requests (predominantly chat generation, sequences >512 tokens) returned truncated or looping output; some streaming sessions stalled. No customer data exfiltration suspected.
- Customer action choices (short): 1) Opt-in to automatic rollforward (we switch you to fallback model variant now), 2) Request replay (we re-run requests against verified model and return results + evidence), 3) Hold - no action (we will continue collecting evidence and advise).

Detailed summary (concise)
- Symptoms observed: elevated structured-output truncation, token repetition, and longer tail latency for streaming sessions starting 2028-04-01 22:07 UTC. Alerts triggered at 22:13 UTC.
- Detection: automated quality-monitoring (prompt set A/B) flagged >40% regression vs baseline for high-length prompts at 22:12 UTC; SRE paging escalated and we began trace collection at 22:20 UTC.
- Initial mitigation: at 22:45 UTC we paused the regional rollout policy for the new routing rule and re-routed new sessions to established capacity. At 23:05 UTC we disabled KV cache sharing between variant families as a precaution.

What we know so far
- Likely cause: a routing rollout introduced a mapping mismatch for quantized variants where two variant families shared cache key namespace. This produced stale KV cache hits for active sessions that expected variant-specific caches. The stale KV entries contained partial past sequences leading to repeated tokens/truncation.
- Scope: affected requests primarily had sequence lengths >512 tokens and used streaming; customers using small prompt lengths or embeddings-only API calls were not affected. Impact window is bounded and small (approx 8.5 hours).
- Data integrity: caches only contained ephemeral model state (KV cache). We have no evidence that customer prompt payloads or stored tenant metadata were accessed or leaked.

Customer recovery choices (details & implications)
1) Automatic rollforward to fallback variant (recommended for most tenants)
   - What we do: immediately move your routed sessions to the verified fallback model variant with independent KV caches and no shared namespace.
   - Benefits: near-immediate mitigation, stops further affected responses.
   - Tradeoffs: slight differences in tokenization/temperature tuning may change some outputs; we log differences and offer post-replay option for critical requests.

2) Replay of impacted requests (auditable evidence package)
   - What we do: with tenant consent we re-run impacted requests against the verified fallback variant (or a pinned model version you specify). We return a replay bundle: original request IDs, timestamps, replayed outputs, and a verification checksum log.
   - Evidence package includes: request ids, original and replayed response payloads, deterministic seeds used, model binary ids and quantization profile, and operator-signed verification manifest.
   - Privacy note: replays are run within your tenant context; we do not share replay payloads outside your tenant. Replays may be throttled to avoid cost spikes; estimate: 2-12 hours depending on volume.

3) No-action hold
   - What we do: continue collecting traces and incremental analysis; notify you when root cause confirmed and when we recommend replay.
   - When to choose: low-touch customers who prefer to wait for a full postmortem before deciding.

How to choose (guidance)
- If your application is customer-facing and long prompts are common - choose option 1 + consider option 2 for high-value requests (e.g., payments, legal text).
- If you operate strict determinism and auditing - request full replay (option 2) and specify a pinned model version for re-evaluation.
- If you saw zero anomalous outputs in your logs - hold is reasonable; we'll flag if evidence indicates latent impact.

Operator timeline (what we have done / will do)
- 2028-04-01 22:13 UTC: quality monitor alert; SRE engaged.
- 2028-04-01 22:45 UTC: paused routing rollout.
- 2028-04-01 23:05 UTC: disabled cross-variant KV namespace; new sessions routed to stable capacity.
- 2028-04-02 01:10 UTC: started evidence collection and deterministic replay harness for sample cohort.
- 2028-04-04 03:00 UTC: candidate root cause identified; patch ready and waiting staged verification.
- Next 24-72 hours: full postmortem + formal RCA with timeline and remediation checklist; we will also publish an integrity verification artifact for tenants who request replays.

Temporary mitigations enacted for all tenants
- Global: halted the rollout that introduced shared cache namespace; instituted a safety check in the routing controller to prevent shared namespaces across variant families.
- Regional (EU): increased observability sampling for long streaming sessions and enabled automatic failover to fallback model.
- Side effect: short-lived increase in tail latency for a minority of requests while sessions migrated - observed median latency unchanged.

Customer-facing artifact options (pick when you respond)
- Minimal: opt-in to automatic rollforward (we do it for you; minimal disruption).
- Audited: request a replay + evidence bundle for impacted request IDs (we provide checksumed artifacts and operator-signed manifest).
- Full forensic: request tenant-specific forensic window (we will open dedicated slot with SRE and provide granular traces and deterministic replays; timeline 3-5 business days).

How to respond (quick actions)
- Reply to this notice with one of: 
   "ROLLFORWARD" (we will switch routing now),
   "REPLAY: [email/proxy/list]" (we will prepare replay bundle and estimate time),
   "HOLD" (no action - please send contact person for follow-up).
- If you need a pinned model for replays include the model id and version. Example: model: redwood-open-13b-vQ/2027-12-07

Evidence and verification (what we will deliver if you request replay)
- Bundle contents: original request ids, original and replay outputs, operator-signed hash manifest, model artifact ids, quantization profile, and seed log.
- Verification note: where nondeterminism exists (e.g., sampling decodes), we include config and seed to reproduce variant. For deterministic modes (greedy/beam) we provide 1:1 checksums.

Customer support & contacts
- Primary CS lead: Sofia Chen (sofia@redwood.ai).
- SRE incident lead: Liam O'Connor (liam@redwood.ai).
- For legal/audit requests: Mariana Torres (mariana@redwood.ai).
- Slack incident thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C02SVC8K/p1680403200000

Notes to self / operator checklist (internal, leave in doc for now)
- Ensure JIRA-INC-2028-975 updated with per-tenant impact lists.
- Build replay-rate estimate script before sending bulk replay opt-ins (cost guardrails).
- Draft public status page blurb (short) after this doc approved by comms.

Appendix: short example of evidence manifest (human readable snippet)
- request_id: req_20280401_0001
- original_ts: 2028-04-01T22:30:12Z
- replay_ts: 2028-04-03T09:04:22Z
- original_model_id: redwood-open-13b-vQ/2027-12-07
- replay_model_id: redwood-open-13b-vQ/2027-12-07-fallback
- quant_profile: q8b-2027-11
- operator_signature: sig-op-2028-04-04-03

END DRAFT - please comment with any phrasing edits or compliance flags.

Unresolved questions (quick)
- Need confirmation from infra if any KV cache namespaces were persisted beyond ephemeral storage (follow-up ticket assigned).
